content: Hi, I've been meaning to tip my toe in Lean again, and thought this could be a start: https://github.com/leanprover/cslib/pull/558 (a simple queue, with amortized complexity proof).

Nice PR. It seems you are using an alternative implementation of the query model using typeclasses instead of inductive types. Some questions, isn’t the potential function rather limited to one operation? And aren’t the operations better expressed inside a state monad that holds the queue?

The potential function takes a state, not an operation, so I think it's fine. I did prefer to have pure operations for simplicity, although now there's basic complexity analysis using amortized costs (and a proof that if amortized cost ≤k \leq k≤k then cost over a sequence of operations is overall bounded by k×length k \times \text{length} k×length + initial potential).
Any chance for a re-review of https://github.com/leanprover/cslib/pull/558 ? Thank you :)
